How the World Fights Traffic Jams: From Cable Cars to AI Traffic Lights

2026-09-22 24KZ (Айгерим Ардаккызы) TomTom, traffic index, Mexico City, congestion, cable cars, AI traffic lights, congestion pricing, New York, China robots, South Korea, urban mobility, traffic management
Read the source article

Quick summary

Kazakh news outlet 24KZ surveys global approaches to fighting traffic congestion using TomTom data, profiling solutions from Mexico City's cable car network to China's robotic lane dividers, South Korea's AI traffic signals, and New York's congestion pricing.

Key takeaways

  • Mexico City has the world's worst traffic at nearly 76% congestion, with drivers losing about 184 hours per year in jams (TomTom data)
  • Mexico City is building three new cable car lines totaling nearly 40 km, with one line expected to cut a 70-minute commute nearly in half
  • China's Zhejiang province uses 18 mobile robotic lane dividers that reconfigure intersections during school rush hours, converting one left-turn lane into two
  • Incheon, South Korea uses AI to analyze traffic flow and optimize signal timing on 25 major roads, achieving a 30% speed increase and halving delay times on a key 6-km stretch
  • New York's congestion pricing (since January 2025, $9 base fare for Manhattan core) reduced traffic by 11% — 27 million fewer cars entering the zone — and generated over $550 million for public transit modernization
  • Global congestion increased by an average of 5 percentage points over the past year according to TomTom
